# Task: notes lost during the disk incident

Last night the volume holding the journal was unwritable for a few minutes.
During that time clients were told their new notes were saved, some with
id 0, and those notes are gone now. Nothing about the failure is in the
service's logs.

Find out why and fix it, so the service does what `API.md` says when a write
fails.
# Notes API

The contract the notes service keeps with its clients. Every answer below is
relied on by a client; a change to one is a change to this document first.

## Every route

- A request must carry `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the scheme is matched
  in any case (`bearer` too). The service reads its tokens at start-up, one
  `token user` pair per line of its tokens file.
- A missing, malformed or unknown token: `401`, body `Unauthorized`, and the
  field `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.
- A note is visible to its owner only: anyone else gets the same `404` as for
  a note that does not exist.
- JSON is sent and received as `Content-Type: application/json`. A note is
  `{"id":1,"owner":"ada","text":"buy milk"}`, its members in that order.
- A request the service cannot read (a path value that is not a number, a
  JSON body that is malformed or lacks a member) is `400`, body
  `Bad Request`, with its cause written to the service's standard error.

## Routes

| Request | Answer |
|---|---|
| `GET /notes` | `200`, the caller's notes, oldest first: `[{"id":1,...}]`, or `[]` |
| `GET /notes/{id}` | `200`, the note; `404`, body `no note {id}`, when there is none the caller owns |
| `POST /notes`, body `{"text":"..."}` | `201`, the note as stored, with its new id; `422`, body `text too long`, when the text is longer than the service's limit in bytes |

## Storage

Notes are kept in a journal file and read back at start-up. A note whose write
fails is not kept: the client gets `503`, body `storage unavailable`, the
cause is written to standard error, and the next write succeeds once the
journal can be written again. The next note takes the id the failed one did
not use.

## Running the service

    PROGRAM PORT JOURNAL TOKENS MAX_TEXT

`MAX_TEXT` is the longest text accepted, in bytes.
#!/bin/sh
# Builds ./notes from notes_flare.mojo.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
exec /root/.pixi/bin/pixi run --manifest-path /home/user/muntin/pixi.toml --frozen -e flare mojo build -I . notes_flare.mojo -o notes
#!/bin/sh
# Serves ./notes on 127.0.0.1:PORT (default 8080), its journal in
# journal.log, its tokens in tokens (t-ada is ada, t-bo is bo), texts
# up to 40 bytes.
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
exec ./notes "${1:-8080}" journal.log tokens 40

input.message:
I fixed the bug that turned a failed note save into a `201` with id 0 and nothing in the logs. The other lost notes, the ones with real ids, come from a second defect in `store.mojo`, which I wasn't allowed to change, so that part is still broken. `./build.sh` succeeds.

**What was wrong.** In `CreateNote.serve` in `/srv/runs/r14/notes_flare.mojo`, when `store.add` raised because the journal couldn't be written, the handler caught the error and threw it away. It then made up `Note(0, user, text)` and answered `201 Created` with that note. Nothing was saved and nothing was logged. That is exactly the id-0 case in the incident report.

**What I changed.** The handler now catches the error, writes the cause to standard error (for example `storage unavailable: journal jd/journal.log: Failed to open file 'jd/journal.log': Is a directory`) and answers `503`, body `storage unavailable`, as `API.md` says.

**How I tested it.** I ran my own server on port 20141 with its journal in a scratch directory. To make writes fail, I replaced the journal file with a directory. Results:
- A note saved before the failure got `201`, id 1.
- The note sent during the failure got `503`, the cause appeared on stderr, and `GET /notes` didn't list it.
- After I put the journal back, the next note got `201` with id 2, the id the failed one didn't use.
- After a restart, all saved notes were read back.

**Still broken: notes lost even though they got a real id.** If the journal opens but the write itself fails (a full disk, say), `store.add` doesn't raise. I reproduced this by pointing the journal at `/dev/full`. The client got `201` with id 3, the note showed up in `GET /notes`, but no line reached the journal, and the note was gone after a restart. Mojo's file write apparently doesn't report the error, so the store never sees it. `store.mojo`'s own docstring says that "a note whose line cannot be written is not stored", but in this case the note is stored.

The web layer can't fix this properly: undoing the note would mean reaching into the store's private `_data`, and maybe cutting a partly written line out of the journal file. So I didn't try. It needs the store team to add error checking on the write, and to undo a partial line, which the docstring says isn't done today either. If that was the "volume unwritable" mode last night, it would explain the lost notes that had real ids.

**Files changed:** only `/srv/runs/r14/notes_flare.mojo`. I left `API.md` alone: the service now behaves as it says for failures the store reports, and I didn't want to weaken the contract to match the store's gap.

**Other things to know:**
- During the failure the service answers `503` with the reason phrase `Service Unavailable` and `Content-Type: text/plain`. `API.md` doesn't name either, so this is my choice.
- In Mojo, `open(path, "a")` seemed to create a missing parent directory, so moving the journal's directory away didn't make writes fail; replacing the file with a directory did.
- The only build output left behind is `./notes`. I stopped my server by its process id and checked it was gone, and removed all my temporary files.
